Fats
Although the total quantity of dietary fat, SFA, and omega-6 
PUFAs do not seem to affect blood pressure (Cicero et al, 2009), 
evidence from short-term feeding trials documented that 
MUFA, when used as a replacement for SFAs, PUFA, or carbo-
hydrate, lowered blood pressure in some individuals with hy-
pertension (Appel et al, 2005). In a large population study 
spanning different continents and diverse dietary patterns, 
higher intake of dietary MUFA (,13 g/day), especially oleic 
acid from plant oils, was associated with significantly lower 
DBP (Miura et al, 2013). In a recent meta-analysis, including 
9 RCTs, examining the effect of MUFA on blood pressure, SBP (net 
change: 22.26 mm Hg), and DBP (net change: 21.15 mm Hg)
